exposure: delivery route (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 281 healthy neonates born between February 2021 and April 2023 at Her Royal Highness Maha Chakri Sirindhorn Medical Center, Srinakharinwirot University, Thailand.
finding: Neonates delivered vaginally exhibited a gut microbiome with higher abundance and diversity than those delivered by cesarean delivery, although Bifidobacterium breve was significantly more abundant in cesarean-delivered neonates.
mod_finding: Route of delivery is associated with neonatal gut microbiome abundance and diversity, with vaginally delivered neonates showing higher diversity but lower abundance of the dominant species (Bifidobacterium breve) compared to cesarean-delivered neonates.
